source: Curated from research/nickel-*-2026-09.md; locality coordinates from the 2024 Census Gazetteer place file

sites.name: Ford Energy Systems, Glendale (former BlueOval SK)
sites.status: Retooling for LFP stationary storage; production planned late 2027
sites.note: Ford reports EV battery production ended in December 2025 and the Kentucky plant is converting to lithium iron phosphate (LFP) storage batteries. LFP does not establish nickel demand; retained as manufacturing context, excluded from nickel-demand distance. The Elizabethtown Census point is about 10 miles from Glendale, not the factory footprint.

sites.name: Ultium Cells, Spring Hill
sites.status: Existing cells plus LFP conversion; nickel demand volume unverified
sites.note: GM says Spring Hill will add LFP alongside existing cells, with commercial LFP production targeted for late 2027. Retained as mixed-chemistry context; not all battery output requires nickel and available nickel offtake is unverified.

sites.name: Ultium Cells, Warren
sites.note: The Ohio Valley anchor of the same corridor.

sites.name: North American Stainless, Ghent
sites.note: The largest integrated US stainless producer, on a 1,400-acre Ohio River site. Stainless is the majority of world nickel demand, though this mill runs heavily on scrap.

sites.name: Eagle Mine
sites.note: The only operating primary nickel-copper mine in the United States. Its concentrate currently leaves the country to be smelted at Sudbury, Ontario — the gap a domestic refinery would close.

sites.name: Humboldt Mill
sites.status: Operating; selected for Tamarack processing September 10, 2026
sites.note: Talon selected its existing Humboldt Mill for Tamarack processing on September 10, 2026. Future Tamarack processing remains dependent on project development; existing plant proximity does not establish available toll-processing capacity.

sites.name: Madison Mine (US Strategic Metals)
sites.note: 1,800-acre cobalt-nickel-copper site 90 miles south of St. Louis, producing concentrate since 2019 with a hydrometallurgical facility near completion.

sites.name: Tamarack nickel-copper project
sites.status: Environmental review; scoping comment period Jul–Sep 2026
sites.note: The most advanced US nickel sulfide deposit in permitting. Talon holds a Tesla agreement for 75,000 t of concentrate.

sites.name: Warren/Union nickel deposit (Exiro)
sites.status: Exploration, apparently stalled since 2023; organised local opposition
sites.note: Nickel-copper-cobalt sulfide around Crawford Pond. No public grade or tonnage. Maine's Chapter 200 rules constrain the mine but explicitly do not reach a refinery.

sites.name: REV Nickel (Revex Technologies)
sites.note: Reprocesses Eagle Mine tailings and spent lithium-ion batteries into nickel concentrate. $145M DOE grant plus $50M from Michigan — the state has already co-funded nickel processing in Marquette County.

sites.name: Kennecott Garfield smelter acid plant
sites.note: One of two operating US copper smelters; its acid plant is a byproduct sulfuric acid source.

sites.name: Freeport-McMoRan Miami smelter acid plant
sites.note: The other operating US copper smelter, and the other byproduct acid source in the West.

sites.name: Central Florida phosphate acid complex
sites.note: Bulk sulfuric acid in the US comes mainly from the Florida and Louisiana phosphate-fertilizer complexes. A hydromet refinery either buys acid here or burns sulfur on site.

sites.name: Port Nickel (former AMAX Metals Recovery)
sites.status: 387-acre tract for sale or lease, listed as of 2026-07-19
sites.note: Built by Freeport Sulphur to refine Moa Bay ore and run as a nickel-cobalt refinery from 1958 to 2000. Deep-water Mississippi dock, Norfolk Southern on an active on-site spur with reciprocal switching, Foreign Trade Zone, in the Gulf Coast sulfuric-acid supply region.

sites.name: Talon Battery Minerals Processing Facility
sites.note: Talon discontinued advancement of the proposed Beulah processing facility after selecting its existing Humboldt Mill in Michigan. Retained as historical project context, not a forthcoming refinery.

sites.name: Westwin Elements nickel refinery
sites.status: Pilot operating; Phase 1 target 18,000 t/yr by 2028
sites.note: The most advanced dedicated US nickel refinery. 480-acre tract in a rail industrial park — the landlocked, rail-fed counterpart to the port-fed model.
